name: Design Library
description: Machine-readable component and template catalog for Habibi/Nexus-style product surfaces.
consumptionGuidance: Load this manifest before generating UI for Nexus, Design Library, or related Unilever internal tools.
Choose existing entries by kind, category, subcategory, useWhen, doNotUseWhen, variants, props, and tokens.
Prefer templates for full-page or block-level composition before assembling primitives from scratch.
Honor doNotUseWhen and accessibility notes as hard constraints during UI generation.
Do not invent components outside this manifest unless the user has approved a gap proposal.

entrySchema.id: Stable identifier used for lookup and references.
entrySchema.category: Top-level catalog category shown in navigation.
entrySchema.props: Documented props or data slots for the implementation.
entrySchema.variants: Supported states, tones, and structural variants.
entrySchema.tokens: Habibi tokens consumed by the entry.
entrySchema.agentGuidance: Composition guidance for AI-assisted UI generation.
entrySchema.code: Copyable implementation snippet or composition starter.
entrySchema.developerHandoff: Source links, import paths, dependencies, and setup notes for developers copying the component.

entries.name: Button
entries.description: Buttons trigger important actions across Design Library surfaces. They use Habibi action tokens, explicit variants, stable sizing, visible focus states, and clear leading, trailing, loading, and icon-only slots.

props.name: variant
props.description: Controls the visual treatment and semantic emphasis.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls height, padding, and text size.

props.name: leadingIcon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: Optional icon rendered after the label.

props.name: loading
props.description: Disables the button and replaces the leading slot with a spinner.

useWhen: Use primary buttons for the single most important action in a region.
Use secondary buttons for supporting actions near a primary action.
Use tertiary buttons for low-emphasis inline actions.
Use destructive buttons only for actions that remove, delete, revoke, or reset.
Use icon-only buttons for compact toolbars when the icon is widely understood and an accessible label is provided.
doNotUseWhen: Do not place multiple primary buttons in the same action group.
Do not use a destructive button for reversible navigation.
Do not rely on icon-only buttons without an accessible label.
Do not use loading buttons without preserving enough width for the action label.
accessibility: Buttons use semantic button elements.
Focus states are visible through the Habibi focus ring.
Loading and disabled states prevent repeated submission.
Icon-only buttons require an aria-label.
Button labels should describe the action, not the destination or generic confirmation.
agentGuidance: Choose one primary button per screen or modal footer.
Pair primary and secondary actions in predictable order: secondary left, primary right.
Prefer action-specific labels like 'Create Agent' or 'Save Changes' instead of generic labels like 'Submit'.
If generating an icon-only action, include aria-label and choose size='icon'.

doNotUseWhen: Do not use Chat Surface for static documentation.

entries.name: Agent Manifest

props.name: kindCounts
props.description: Entry totals by component, foundation, and template.

props.name: categoryCounts
props.description: Entry totals for each navigation category.

props.name: consumptionGuidance
props.description: Rules for AI agents consuming the catalog.

props.name: entrySchema
props.description: Plain-language schema map for every manifest entry.

useWhen: Load the manifest before generating Design Library UI.
Select entries by kind, category, subcategory, props, variants, tokens, and agent guidance.
Use templates first for full-page or block-level UI before composing primitives manually.
doNotUseWhen: Do not scrape visual docs when the manifest is available.

agentGuidance: Fetch the manifest, choose from approved entries, and honor useWhen, doNotUseWhen, props, variants, tokens, and accessibility notes.
Use categoryCounts and kindCounts to understand coverage before deciding whether a request is a component, foundation, or template task.
For templates, copy composition patterns before inventing new layouts.

developerHandoff.packageInstallCommand: No package install required for the manifest endpoint.
requiredSetup: Fetch-capable runtime or server route
JSON parser
Use entry IDs, props, variants, tokens, and guidance before generating UI

entries.name: Team Workspace Home
entries.description: A workspace landing page combining shell navigation, health, launchers, shortcuts, notifications, recent items, and activity.
useWhen: Use as a starting page for cross-project teams and design-library workspaces.
Use when users need to resume work and launch frequent actions.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for single-purpose tools that have no workspace switching or recent work.
Do not overload the home page with every available action.
accessibility: Navigation, recent items, notifications, and actions keep visible labels.
Status and health states include text.
agentGuidance: Compose with Navigation Header, Health Summary, App Launcher, Shortcut Grid, Saved Report Card, Notification Menu, Recent Items, and Activity Feed.
Use this template for team home pages and workspace landing screens.

entries.name: Mobile Agent Chat
entries.description: A narrow-screen agent chat surface with conversation header, status bar, suggestions, evidence, and mobile tab navigation.
useWhen: Use when an agent workflow needs a responsive or mobile-first preview.
Use when evidence must stay available even on narrow screens.
doNotUseWhen: Do not use for desktop-only dashboards.
Do not hide source evidence behind unlabeled navigation when claims require review.
accessibility: Conversation, suggestions, evidence, and navigation keep visible text labels.
Icon-only actions come from labelled primitives.
agentGuidance: Compose with Conversation Header, Agent Status Bar, Chat Surface, Chat Message, Suggestion Chips, Composer, Evidence List, and Mobile Tab Bar.
Use this template for mobile agent experiences and responsive QA checks.
